title: Deterministic discount policy reaches for HTTP and the filesystem directly

consumerGuidance.architecture: Shop.Pricing holds deterministic money policy. IBlackoutCalendar and ITierConfiguration already exist as injected seams and are registered for exactly this purpose.
consumerGuidance.notes: DiscountPolicy is called synchronously from the checkout request path. Its unit tests run in CI with no network access.

mustCite: the HttpClient constructed inside Apply and the File.ReadAllText call beside it
the existing IBlackoutCalendar and ITierConfiguration seams the project already registers
the consequence that checkout pricing now depends on an outbound call and a local file that the policy neither owns nor declares
the correction of taking the existing seams as constructor dependencies
that the tier and expiry rules are deterministic and were previously testable without setup
that the existing unit tests now require network and filesystem state CI does not provide
the consequence that a money rule can no longer be exercised in isolation
the correction of restoring the injected seams rather than adding test infrastructure
the new failure behavior, where a blackout-calendar request failure throws out of Apply into the checkout request
that no test covers that failure path for the affected contract
the consequence that a calendar outage fails checkout with an unhandled exception
a correction naming the contract to protect or the failure behavior to define

acceptableAdditionalFindings: Constructing a new HttpClient per call rather than using IHttpClientFactory, with the socket-exhaustion consequence stated.
The synchronous .Result inside Apply, if reported with its own call site and consequence.

forbiddenFindings.example: Re-reviewing the test suite's assertion style or coverage percentage, or citing the 214 passing tests as evidence that the policy is sound.
Requiring a repository, hexagonal project split or DDD domain service for pricing.
Objecting to the static method or to the hard-coded path string's formatting.

notes: The project already has the seams, which is what makes the hidden dependency a defect rather than a design preference. The test finding is scoped to the affected contract's failure path so it does not become a second test review.
